summary: Pre-alpha (Step 91): the headless CLI (file inspection, image assets of Markdown documents) and the editor window (editing, files, Markdown preview, Ctrl+V images)

commands.name: capabilities
commands.summary: This document

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Jarak's version and the contract and schema versions it speaks

commands.name: paths
commands.summary: Where Jarak keeps its settings, session and recovery files; reads nothing and creates nothing

commands.name: open
commands.summary: Start the Jarak window (jarak-gui.exe next to jarak.exe) with these files or a folder (the workspace), or hand them to the running window; a missing file opens as a new document and is created only when you save

commands.name: info
commands.summary: A file's encoding, byte-order mark, line endings, size and line count, and whether Jarak can save it unchanged (lossless) or opens it read-only; changes nothing

commands.name: find
commands.summary: The matches of a text, an escaped text or a regular expression in a file or in a folder's files (Notepad++-style filters, sub-folders, hidden folders; binary files skipped) with their line and column (at most 10 000 listed); changes nothing

commands.name: replace
commands.summary: Replace in Files: --dry-run lists every change and writes nothing; with --yes each file is checked against the plan, its original bytes journaled, and saved atomically in its own encoding, byte-order mark and line endings; lossy, binary and unencodable files are skipped

commands.name: export
commands.summary: Exports locally: highlighted text as HTML or RTF, a Markdown document rendered as HTML with its images embedded (or linked), or published to a folder with copies of its images, or PDF through Microsoft Print to PDF (--to pdf); nothing is fetched or uploaded; the document is never changed and an existing output is replaced only with --overwrite

commands.name: print
commands.summary: Prints with the print settings on the default printer or --printer (a Markdown document rendered, other text highlighted); a printer that writes a file (Microsoft Print to PDF) needs --output; no dialog ever opens; --dry-run lays out the pages and prints nothing

commands.name: printers
commands.summary: The printers Windows knows, the default one and those that write a file; changes nothing

commands.name: journal.list
commands.summary: The Replace in Files batches kept for undo (the newest 20), with their files; changes nothing

commands.name: journal.undo
commands.summary: Gives the files of a Replace in Files batch their original bytes back, leaving any file changed since the batch as it is

commands.name: assets.list
commands.summary: The images a Markdown document refers to (found, missing, remote, outside its folder) and the files in its assets folder no Markdown file there refers to; changes and deletes nothing

commands.name: assets.rename
commands.summary: Renames an image asset of a Markdown document and rewrites the document's references to it (encoding and line endings kept); never replaces a file and refuses an asset other documents in the folder use

commands.name: settings.list
commands.summary: Every setting of settings.toml (or one section's) with its value, its default and what values it takes; changes nothing

commands.name: settings.get
commands.summary: One setting's value (the default when the file does not set it, or sets a value it does not take); changes nothing

commands.name: settings.set
commands.summary: Checks the value against the setting and writes it into settings.toml atomically, keeping the file's other lines; a running window applies it when it gets the focus

commands.name: settings.reset
commands.summary: Removes the setting's line from settings.toml, so its default applies

commands.name: hotkeys.list
commands.summary: Every remappable command with its keys (the user's or the defaults), where they come from and conflicts (the shared hotkey contract); changes nothing

commands.name: hotkeys.show
commands.summary: One command's keys and conflicts; changes nothing

commands.name: hotkeys.set
commands.summary: Gives a command these keys in hotkeys.json (checked by the hotkey contract: syntax, reserved keys, conflicts — another of the user's bindings only with --replace); written atomically

commands.name: hotkeys.disable
commands.summary: The command gets no keys (hotkeys.json)

commands.name: hotkeys.reset
commands.summary: The command's default keys again (its override leaves hotkeys.json)

commands.name: hotkeys.check
commands.summary: Conflicts of Jarak's shortcuts with each other and with keys Windows, Kim and the input method reserve; changes nothing
